summary.title: NOSQL Patterns
summary.one_liner: A design-patterns overview of large-scale NoSQL key-value stores covering consistent hashing, replication models, quorum reads/writes, vector clocks, gossip, and storage engine techniques.
keywords: how do nosql databases partition data
takeaways: Consistent hashing on a ring limits key redistribution when nodes join or crash, compared with key mod N partitioning.
Replication choices (single master vs multi-master) determine how updates propagate and how workload is spread.
Quorum settings with W + R > N give strict consistency; smaller values trade consistency for availability and performance.
Vector clocks and gossip let replicas reason about causal order and converge to the same state eventually.
Storage techniques like CouchDB's append-only copy-on-write and BigTable's memtable plus bloom filters support scalable writes and reads.
summary.summary: This long blog post, written in 2009, describes common design patterns behind large-scale NoSQL key-value stores such as Dynamo, Voldemort, Cassandra, Riak, BigTable, and CouchDB. It walks through the key/value API, partitioning with consistent hashing and virtual nodes, membership changes, and replication under master-slave and multi-master models. It then covers client consistency models, quorum-based reads and writes, vector clocks, gossip-based state and operation transfer, delete handling, and storage engine designs. The text is an informal set of notes rather than a tutorial with code.
